text:
sam: Running the stream-sampling probe on canary today. Seeing a repeating micro-stall pattern — ~120ms blips every 8th chunk for long tails. Not sure if this is kernel selection thrash or KV cache alignment. Attaching quick probe snippet below.

anya: Can you paste the emit interval histogram? Is it correlated with sequence length or batch boundaries?

sam: Paste from the probe: ```emit_interval_ms: [0-5ms: 7200, 5-20ms: 1800, 20-80ms: 210, 80-140ms: 48, 140-300ms: 2] chunk_index_mod8_spike: true``` Looks like the 80-140ms bucket maps to chunk_index % 8 == 0.

kevin: Interesting. We recently changed batcher packing to prefer power-of-two minibatches for kernel alignment on A100s — could be an alignment artifact where KV cache flushes or kernel swap happens on those boundaries.

liz: Also check client vs server timestamps — client-side chunk ACKs might be delayed if jitter accumulates. Sam, can you include client-side send_ts vs server_emit_ts?

sam: Added a short diff from logs: ```client_send_ts: [t0,t1,t2,...], server_emit_ts: [t0+1,t1+2,t2+1,...] but at chunk_index % 8 we see server_emit_ts - client_send_ts jump by ~120ms.```

kevin: That screams kernel warmup or a short preemption. Which kernel variant is being chosen for those batches? Are we switching between fp16-kern-V1 and quant-kern-V2 at runtime?

sam: According to the selection trace: chunk 0..6 -> quant-kern-V2, chunk 7 -> fallback to fp16-kern-V1 with slower memcpy path. The runtime fallback log shows: `kernel_select: quant-kern-V2 failed heuristics -> scale to fp16-kern-V1` for those chunks.

anya: Why would heuristics flip only on that chunk index? Could be batching heuristic combining a cold request with a hot prefix, or the KV cache eviction boundary. Any evictions logged near that time?

sam: KV profiler shows a tiny eviction burst right before the spike: `kvcache_evictions: +3 at t=...` Possibly prefix cache pressure triggers selection to a kernel that avoids kv-lookup vectorization.

liz: Two hypotheses: 1) Batching heuristic groups that request into a different packing that triggers fallback kernel, 2) KV eviction causes kernel route that is slower.

kevin: Quick test: force kernel override to quant-kern-V2 for that trace and see if spike disappears. If yes, we know selection is the problem. Sam, can you run a probe with `--force-kernel=quant-kern-V2` on the same workload?

sam: Running now. perfbot: schedule?

perfbot: perf-probe job queued id=4523, executing on canary pool.

sam: Probe done. Results: emit_interval 80-140ms bucket dropped to 1 count (was 48). client vs server delta flattened. No eviction logged.

anya: That is pretty conclusive — kernel selection leading to a slow path. Next: why did selection flip? We should capture the exact heuristic inputs (seq_len, pad_ratio, kv_hotness, batch_layout).

kevin: I pushed a quick guard to the heuristic: avoid switching kernels mid-request based on ephemeral pad_ratio changes. PR in flight: r/eng-runtime#2314. Can someone run regression probe?

liz: Running a 1h sampling harness now against the canary route. Will post dashboard once done.

sam: Dashboard snippet: `per_route_emit_p99: 38ms -> 39ms (before patch), 38ms -> 36ms (after patch on canary)`, stream-stall events per 10k chunks: 7 -> 1.

kevin: Nice. Follow-ups: 1) Add a token-level label in traces when kernel fallback occurs so we can correlate in dashboards. 2) Add a kv-eviction counter as a redline for the stream dashboard.

anya: Also add a small alert if emit_interval histogram shows a persistent secondary peak >50ms. Use :eyes: threshold for customer-facing routes.

perfbot: created issue PERF-876: "token-level kernel-fallback label + kv-eviction redline" and linked to r/eng-runtime#2314.

sam: TL;DR: micro-stalls were caused by kernel-selection fallback triggered by ephemeral heuristic inputs, exacerbated by occasional KV evictions. For now we have a heuristic guard, a forced-kernel probe validated fix, and a dashboard/alert workitem.

liz: Nice work. I'll keep the canary running for 24h and then roll to staging if clean.

kevin: If canary stays clean, let's schedule a dedicated capacity patch to prevent similar heuristic oscillations on high-throughput routes.

sam: Thanks team. Filing the postmortem note in the perf board. :thumbsup:
